clue.text: 4 plus 9 minus 1 could give this number

definitions.note: read as numb-er: something that numbs, i.e. a painkiller

indicators.note: minus says these letters are taken away from the pool of the two spelt-out numbers
could give suggests the remaining letters might be rearranged to produce something new

parts.note: the figure 4 is written out as the word four
the figure 9 is written out as the word nine
one in Roman numerals is I

explanation.surface: A simple sum, 4 plus 9 minus 1, apparently producing some number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus' takes I (Roman one) out of FOURNINE and 'could give' rearranges what is left. 'number' is not a figure but a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurofen is a brand of ibuprofen painkiller, and a painkiller deadens pain, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: Innovator with logs raised an outstanding platform

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word an is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a pier is a platform standing out into the sea

explanation.surface: A woodworking innovator with logs builds a raised, impressive platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logs' suggests timber, but means logarithms; 'outstanding' means projecting, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: John Napier, the Scottish mathematician, invented logarithms, the mathematical tool known as logs.

clue.text: Charge around, returning to participate in revolution

indicators.note: around says the charge word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

indicators.note: returning means the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Rebels charging about, coming back to take part in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political uprising, but means turning in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that takes part in a revolution in the turning sense spins about an axis.

clue.text: Main high jumper prone to interrupt fellows roughly

indicators.note: to interrupt says the prone word breaks into the fellows letters

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural
prone means lying face down
-ish is a suffix meaning roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: An athletic high jumper, prone on the mat, breaks into a rough crowd of fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not 'chief': this jumper leaps out of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying fish leap out of the water and glide above the waves, so they are leapers of the sea.

clue.text: Fresh head of lettuce after fifteen days?

indicators.note: after says the lettuce letter follows the fifteen-day piece

parts.note: November has thirty days, so its first half, the letters NOVE, makes fifteen days

indicators.note: head of says take the first letter of the word lettuce

explanation.surface: Is a lettuce still fresh after a fortnight or so in the fridge?
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags a whimsical piece: half of the word November, a thirty-day month, stands for fifteen days.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means new and original, which is one sense of fresh.

clue.text: Female with useless fellow, flipping tool

indicators.note: flipping means the words for the useless fellow are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a waster is a good-for-nothing, a useless person

explanation.surface: A woman with a good-for-nothing man, plus a mild expletive about a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse on 'tool', but it turns WASTER round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw used for cutting intricate shapes in wood, a woodworking implement.

clue.text: Deceit cut cocaine supply for mathematician

parts.note: a fib is a small lie, a deceit

indicators.note: supply read as supple-y, i.e. bent into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
cut means the word cocaine loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A dealer's lie about the purity of his cocaine supply, in a story about a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like the dealer's adulteration but drops the last letter of COCAINE; 'supply' is read as an adjective (suppler) and rearranges COCAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo Fibonacci was a medieval Italian mathematician, famous for his number sequence.

clue.text: Where to flog horse mounted by earl

indicators.note: mounted by in a down clue puts the earl letter on top of the horse word

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Where to whip a horse being ridden by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' suggests whipping the horse, but it is slang for sell.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is an online auction site, and to flog in British slang is to sell.

clue.text: What drug dealer may do in kitchen vessel

definitions.meaning: a dealer may ..., keeping a supply of cannabis
a large pan for making stock

explanation.surface: A drug dealer hiding his stash in a cooking pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a deep pan in which soup stock is simmered, a cooking container.

clue.text: Traveller much easier on the eye, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken and the letters entered are another spelling of that sound

parts.note: way means much, as in way better; fairer means more attractive, easier to look at

explanation.surface: A traveller who is far more attractive than others, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, an old word for a traveller.

clue.text: Run away from lovely Mickey Mouse

indicators.note: away from says the letter for run is removed from the word for lovely

parts.note: pretty means lovely, attractive
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An instruction to flee from an adorable cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mickey Mouse' as an adjective means trivial or amateurish, not the cartoon mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse is informal for trifling or second-rate, much as petty means small and unimportant.

clue.text: Shaking cups in triumph, after eliminating clubs

indicators.note: in places the word for cups inside the shortened triumph word
after eliminating says the clubs letter is removed from the word for triumph first

parts.note: a victory is a triumph
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a bra is a garment made of cups

explanation.surface: A trembling hand holding trophy cups at a moment of sporting triumph, once clubs are knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after eliminating' turns VICTORY into VITORY before 'in' does its work. 'cups' suggests trophies, but means a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibratory describes something vibrating, which is a rapid shaking or trembling motion.

clue.text: Catching in net at sea, seeking fish

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the word net is jumbled

parts.note: angling is trying to catch fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A trawler catching things in a net out at sea while hunting fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is the anagram signal, turning NET into ENT; 'Catching in net' looks like the definition but only 'Catching' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangling means snaring or trapping something so it cannot get free, a way of catching it.

clue.text: President has answer for specialists in assembly

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A president with an answer for experts in a legislative assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' suggests a parliament, but means putting together flat-pack furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: IKEA sells flat-pack furniture that customers must put together themselves, so the firm is all about home assembly.

clue.text: Clean bumfluff?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically: bum means sponge (scrounge) and fluff means down

explanation.surface: A cleaning instruction for adolescent downy facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumfluff is British slang for a teenager's first wispy beard; the '?' warns it splits as bum (to sponge) plus fluff (down).
explanation.definitionFit: Sponging down a surface wipes it with a wet sponge, a way of cleaning it.

clue.text: Call on General de Gaulle, for one

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the call word comes after the General's name

parts.note: General Franco was the Spanish dictator
to phone someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A request to telephone the French general Charles de Gaulle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' points at de Gaulle in the surface, but the general in the wordplay is Spain's Franco.
explanation.definitionFit: De Gaulle was a French speaker, and a francophone is anyone whose language is French.

clue.text: Puzzled man at home when the penny drops

indicators.note: puzzled means confused, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bewildered man sitting at home until he finally understands.
explanation.definitionFit: An aha moment is a sudden insight, just as the penny dropping is the idiom for finally understanding.

clue.text: Green food: the thing in cooked apples

indicators.note: in puts the thing word inside the rearranged letters
cooked suggests the apples are worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it means the thing

explanation.surface: A healthy-eating tip: the key ingredient in cooked apples is something green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes SPLPEA, and 'in' splits it after SPL. 'Green food' fits the apples of the surface, a decoy for the pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried green peas halved for soups and dal, a green foodstuff.

clue.text: It's close to Vietnam, place in eastern region

definitions.text: It's close to Vietnam, place in eastern region

indicators.note: close to means take the final letter of Vietnam
in puts the word for place inside the eastern region

parts.note: Asia is the eastern continent
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: A geography note: a country near Vietnam, located in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the country, and also builds it: 'close to' gives the last letter of Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia is a Southeast Asian country lying across the South China Sea from Vietnam.

clue.text: Console Victoria, say, after large cuts in income

indicators.note: after says the station word follows the other piece
cuts in says the letter for large slices its way into the income word

parts.note: pay is income from work
Victoria is a major London railway station

explanation.surface: Comforting someone called Victoria after big cuts to her income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a verb meaning comfort, but it is the noun: a games console. Victoria is a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The PlayStation is Sony's video-games machine, and such machines are called games consoles.

clue.text: Perhaps one's taken in drink

indicators.note: taken in says the one letter goes inside the drink word

parts.note: water is a drink
one is the Roman numeral I; read one's as one has

explanation.surface: A server who has carried drinks in, or perhaps one who has had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one's' as 'one has': one (I) has been taken into WATER. The whole clue also hints at the answer: a server carrying drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter brings food and drink to diners, so drinks are something a waiter takes in.

clue.text: See what's in thus?

indicators.note: in says the what word goes inside the word for how thus is printed

parts.note: in the printed puzzle the word thus is set in bold type, so thus stands for bold
eh? is a way of asking what? when you did not hear

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what is contained in the word thus.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is typographical: in the newspaper the word 'thus' appeared in bold print, so 'thus' means BOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old-fashioned command to look, a literary synonym of see.

clue.text: Tablet yours truly had to swallow every year

indicators.note: to swallow says the yours-truly-had letters take the yearly abbreviation inside

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying I, me
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd
PA is the abbreviation of per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Someone admits they had to swallow a pill every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests a pill, but it is a tablet computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPad is Apple's tablet computer, the best-known example of that kind of device.

clue.text: Shocked look is what Betty and Scott have, stripped naked

parts.note: both names contain a double T

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters of naked are peeled away, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A startled glance at Betty and Scott, caught completely naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' looks like it belongs with 'naked' in the surface, but it removes the outer letters of NAKED to leave AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a delayed second glance of surprise, the classic look of someone shocked.

clue.text: Steer north through curvy region with big curves

indicators.note: through puts the reversed steer letters inside the curvy region word

parts.note: the bum is a rounded part of the body

indicators.note: north in a down clue means the word for steer is read upwards

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: Driving a vehicle north through a winding stretch of country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb about driving but is the animal; 'north' turns OX into XO.
explanation.definitionFit: Buxom describes a woman with a full, curvaceous figure, especially a large bust.

clue.text: Area covered by Scottish hill runner, perhaps

indicators.note: covered by says the area letter sits inside the hill word

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A fell runner on a Scottish hillside covering a stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but a runner bean is a climbing vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Runner beans are a common climbing variety, so a runner is one example of a bean.

clue.text: Choreographed a sexed-up Boxing Day dance

indicators.note: Boxing means the jumbled letters enclose the letter for day
choreographed means arranged into new steps, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy dance routine arranged for Boxing Day, the British holiday after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choreographed' rearranges A SEXEDUP; 'Boxing' puts D inside. Boxing Day is the British holiday of 26 December, here split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de deux is a ballet dance for two performers, typically a duet in classical ballet.

clue.text: Piece of trout, rotten piece at the end

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of decaying fish, the last scrap left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An outro is the closing section of a song or programme, the counterpart of an intro.

clue.text: V & A acquires ultimate piece of art

parts.note: to gain something is to acquire it

indicators.note: ultimate piece of says take the last letter of the word art

explanation.surface: The Victoria and Albert Museum in London buys a final work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V & A' looks like the London museum, but the V alone is the definition and the A is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: V is short for versus, Latin for against, as in a match between two sides.

clue.text: Dressed football team like Liverpool

parts.note: Man U is the informal name for Manchester United football club
Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds and play in red

explanation.surface: One football team dressed up to look like their rivals Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' suggests clothing, but here it is the gardener's sense: spread with fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners dress soil with fertiliser; spreading dung over it is that kind of top dressing.
